extracted.intended_audience: independent documentary filmmakers and producers seeking funding for feature-length nonfiction projects that engage with science and culture
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and selection criteria for applying to the Sundance Institute Sandbox Fund (administered with Sandbox Films) which supports feature-length nonfiction documentary projects that connect science and culture. Covers eligibility, application method, timeline, grant amounts, and creative considerations used in selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose / mission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sandbox Fund offers grants, engagement events, and other opportunities for independent artists seeking to explore the intrinsic link between science and culture through innovative storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administered by the Sundance Institute Documentary Fund in collaboration with Sandbox Films; supports nonfiction projects that inspire a deeper interest in science, especially among those who don’t think of themselves as science enthusiasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — project type
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. and international feature-length nonfiction projects are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects must be feature-length nonfiction (documentary) to qualify; no further format exceptions stated on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — applicant profile / thematic focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are offered to independent artists who are working at the intersection of science and nonfiction storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The partnership identifies and supports nonfiction projects that inspire a deeper interest in science, especially among audiences who don’t already consider themselves science enthusiasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted through the Sandbox Fund application portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions sent by other means or to other contacts are not indicated as acceptable; follow the portal process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline & decision schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fund offers grants two times a year, with two separate application windows; grant-making decisions occur generally in the winter and summer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example cycle: 2026 Spring Cycle opens March 23, 2026 with deadline April 13, 2026. Applicants will be notified within 4–6 months of the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stages supported
rubrics_metrics.description: The fund offers support to projects at all stages of development, production, and post-production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly lists development, production, and post-production as eligible stages for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical grant sizes / funding levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Average grant sizes are as follows: Development (up to $40,000); Production (up to $100,000); Post-Production (up to $100,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are presented as typical/average maximum amounts; actual awards may vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection / creative considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection criteria will emphasize creative narrative techniques and projects that highlight diversity in science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically favors projects that feature characters, topics, or disciplines that broaden and redefine what it means to be a scientist or to do science; emphasis on innovative storytelling that connects science and culture.
